items.answer: The statement is valid. It contains dust particles and water vapour, and all changes in weather and climate take place in it.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (it contains dust particles and water vapour, and all changes in weather and climate take place in it.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: In the study of the composition of the atmosphere, the term 'water vapour' refers to:
items.answer: The variable gaseous form of water in the atmosphere, up to 4 per cent by volume in warm and wet tropics

options: The momentary state of the atmosphere at a place
A gas found mainly between 10 and 50 km above the earth's surface that absorbs ultraviolet rays of the sun
The lowermost layer of the atmosphere, about 13 km thick on average, in which all weather changes take place
The variable gaseous form of water in the atmosphere, up to 4 per cent by volume in warm and wet tropics

items.stem:
Statement: Temperature, pressure, winds and humidity are studied together.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: They are interrelated elements, and a change in one affects the others.
items.markingKey: (b) They are interrelated elements, and a change in one affects the others.
options: Strong convectional currents at the equator carry heat to greater heights.
They are interrelated elements, and a change in one affects the others.
It is transparent to incoming solar radiation but absorbs outgoing terrestrial radiation.
It is the average of weather conditions over a long period of time.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Ozone is important for life on earth.
items.answer: It absorbs ultraviolet rays of the sun and prevents them from reaching the surface.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: It absorbs ultraviolet rays of the sun and prevents them from reaching the surface. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the structure of the atmosphere and answer the questions that follow.
"The stratosphere contains the ozone layer. The air temperature at the tropopause is about minus 80°C over the equator and about minus 45°C over the poles. Density of air is highest near the earth's surface and decreases rapidly with height."
(i) The ozone layer is found in the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'troposphere' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The stratosphere is important for life. (1)
items.answer: (i) stratosphere (ii) The lowermost layer of the atmosphere, about 13 km thick on average, in which all weather changes take place. (iii) It contains the ozone layer, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation and shields life from intense harmful energy.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) stratosphere (ii) The lowermost layer of the atmosphere, about 13 km thick on average, in which all weather changes take place. (iii) It contains the ozone layer, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation and shields life from intense harmful energy.

items.stem: Which gas forms the largest share of the atmosphere by volume?
items.answer: Nitrogen
items.markingKey: (a) Nitrogen.
options: Nitrogen
Argon
Carbon dioxide
Oxygen

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the structure of the atmosphere:
I. The atmosphere consists of layers with different density and temperature.
II. The air temperature at the tropopause is about minus 80°C over the equator and about minus 45°C over the poles.
III. The ionosphere lies below the stratosphere.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: The ionosphere lies above the mesosphere, between about 80 and 400 km.
options: I only
I and II only
III only
All of them

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the atmosphere:
I. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has been rising because of the burning of fossil fuels.
II. Dust particles are generally concentrated in the lower layers of the atmosphere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the elements of weather and climate:
I. Weather does not change during a day.
II. The main elements of weather and climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation.
III. The elements of weather and climate are interrelated.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Weather changes quickly, even within a day. II is correct. III is correct.
options: All of them
II and III only
III only
II only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the elements of weather and climate and answer the questions that follow.
"Weather changes quickly, even within a day or week. Climate changes very slowly and may remain unchanged for 50 years or more. The main elements of weather and climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation."
(i) The momentary state of the atmosphere at a place is called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'elements of weather' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Temperature, pressure, winds and humidity are studied together. (1)
items.answer: (i) weather (ii) Temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation, which together describe weather and climate. (iii) They are interrelated elements, and a change in one affects the others.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) weather (ii) Temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation, which together describe weather and climate. (iii) They are interrelated elements, and a change in one affects the others.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the atmosphere:
I. Temperature increases with height in the troposphere.
II. The troposphere is thickest at the poles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Neither I nor II
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: It decreases at about 1°C for every 165 m of height. II is incorrect: It is thickest at the equator (about 18 km) because heat is carried up by strong convection.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the composition of the atmosphere and answer the questions that follow.
"Subtropical and temperate regions have more dust particles than equatorial and polar regions because of dry winds. Water vapour absorbs part of the insolation and also preserves the earth's radiated heat. The atmosphere is a mixture of many gases along with water vapour and dust particles."
(i) The proportion of water vapour in the atmosphere can be as high as 4 per cent by volume in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'water vapour' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Water vapour helps keep the earth from becoming too hot or too cold. (1)
items.answer: (i) warm and wet tropics (ii) The variable gaseous form of water in the atmosphere, up to 4 per cent by volume in warm and wet tropics. (iii) It absorbs part of the insolation and preserves the earth's radiated heat, acting like a blanket.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) warm and wet tropics (ii) The variable gaseous form of water in the atmosphere, up to 4 per cent by volume in warm and wet tropics. (iii) It absorbs part of the insolation and preserves the earth's radiated heat, acting like a blanket.
